decode.structure: text-record handshake ({0,guid,seq,...}); the client ASSIGNS the ack/connection GUID (77393350-...) at cli frame 3 and the manager adopts it; the manager ORIGINATES 5 session GUIDs (e23134a2, 7f58f27d, ae135932, d450256e, 102301e1) in its first frames

experiment: regenerate the 5 manager-originated GUIDs fresh (preseed_guid_map) while learning the client-assigned GUIDs as usual

result.conclusion: FAILS: regenerating the manager-originated handshake GUIDs makes the client reject the session (248 uniform-665, card never opens). Adaptive replay with the CAPTURED manager GUIDs works on a fresh TestClient, so the GUIDs are not arbitrary - the client validates/correlates them (a challenge/response or derivation not yet decoded). The 7-frame handshake is therefore the irreducible replay: it must be replayed with captured manager GUIDs, while everything after it (operations, navigation incl. arbitrary length, polls, writes) is synthesized from templates.

practical_limit: the Python manager drives the flow as: replay the 7-frame handshake (captured manager GUIDs) + synthesize every subsequent frame (template + live/learned GUID rebind + fresh nonce) + minimize polls (252 frames). The handshake decode (deeper challenge/response structure) is a separate follow-up.
